title: Reliable oral systemic exposure for folded peptides and proteins

concept.text: The innovation would be a generalizable molecular or formulation approach that allows swallowed peptides and proteins to reach the bloodstream intact, biologically functional and at predictable therapeutic exposure. It would protect the medicine through the gastrointestinal environment and enable absorption across the gastrointestinal epithelium. The intended advance is a transferable delivery capability across structurally different drugs, extending beyond a formulation that works for one unusually suitable peptide.

The scope is systemic treatment through gastrointestinal absorption. Medicines that act locally inside the gut address a separate delivery goal. Swallowed devices that inject a payload into gastrointestinal tissue also use a distinct mechanism and are excluded from this molecular or formulation concept. Reliable exposure must include retained drug function: detecting protein-derived material in blood would not by itself demonstrate delivery of an active medicine.

significance.text: Gastrointestinal degradation and poor epithelial permeability constrain oral systemic delivery of peptide and protein medicines, leaving many dependent on injections. A broadly transferable solution could give many existing antibody, enzyme, cytokine and peptide treatments an oral administration option. Its revolutionary importance would lie in changing how a large class of medicines can be delivered, without requiring a new disease target or a new therapeutic mechanism for every application.

Reduced injection burden would follow directly for treatments successfully converted to oral dosing. Better adherence, wider access and improved outcomes would be conditional benefits, depending on affordability, safety, dosing convenience, patient behavior and the amount of drug required. Matching injected efficacy would additionally require retained biological activity, an appropriate concentration-versus-time profile and clinical validation. Oral administration alone does not improve therapeutic precision, therapeutic index or safety, and each disease would still require an effective molecule.

Synthesis: the important practical advance would be predictable, usable exposure across diverse medicines, rather than achieving a particular absorption percentage in isolation. Low bioavailability can be workable for a potent, long-lived drug, while a higher absorbed fraction could still be inadequate if exposure is erratic, drug function is lost or manufacturing enough material is impractical. No fixed percentage bioavailability threshold is adopted here.

missing_breakthrough.text: The unsolved capability is a transferable way to overcome several barriers together. Acidic conditions and gastrointestinal proteases can destroy or inactivate the payload before absorption. The epithelium, including its restrictive tight junctions, strongly limits macromolecular passage. First-pass metabolism can further reduce systemic availability. A formulation must therefore preserve intact, functional drug while enabling sufficient epithelial transport and surviving the losses that occur before the drug reaches the systemic circulation.

Predictability is a separate engineering challenge from obtaining occasional absorption. Food, water volume and dosing conditions can substantially affect exposure, and variability within and between patients can make a nominally successful formulation unreliable. Broad applicability also requires accommodating proteins with different structures and pharmacological requirements. A delivery method that works for a small, engineered peptide does not establish that a larger folded protein will cross the same barriers while retaining activity.

These barriers establish a difficult unmet capability, not a proof that future approaches are impossible. The March 2026 review emphasizes semaglutide's long half-life and accumulation, but lack of substantial accumulation alone does not rule out therapeutic exposure for another drug. Under linear pharmacokinetics, average steady-state concentration depends on the absorbed dose rate and clearance. The remaining questions include whether an adequate dose can be absorbed safely and consistently, and whether its resulting peaks and troughs are clinically suitable.

current_state.text: Niazi's review, published on March 20, 2026, reports oral semaglutide as an approved medicine and interprets it as a molecule-specific success rather than validation of a general protein-delivery platform. It describes a favorable combination of high potency, a roughly one-week half-life, a sufficiently wide therapeutic window and pharmacological effects compatible with low, variable absorption. This demonstrates that an oral peptide can be clinically useful; it does not establish a general rule for folded proteins or quantify how many other proteins could share the necessary properties.

The supplied review reports approximately 0.4–1 percent absolute oral bioavailability for semaglutide under restricted administration conditions involving fasting, limited water and a delay before food. The retained FDA clinical pharmacology extract independently corroborates this range as a population-pharmacokinetic estimate, along with an approximately one-week half-life and substantial effects of administration conditions. The range should not be presented as an uncomplicated direct measurement: the FDA discussion notes assay limitations in early direct bioavailability measurements.

The March review describes trial histories involving insulin, calcitonin, parathyroid-hormone fragments, growth hormone and other oral peptide programs, without identifying a general commercial solution. These histories remain secondary reporting in the supplied evidence. Detailed assertions about the oral parathyroid-hormone and growth-hormone programs warrant particular caution because the cited references identified in the review concern general osteoclast biology and growth-hormone biology, respectively, rather than clearly substantiating those program histories. That weakness leaves the program details uncertain; it does not establish that the programs or reported results are false.

The review also describes advances in specific oral macrocyclic peptide programs. Such molecule-specific successes are relevant evidence that oral peptide delivery can be engineered for selected structures, but they do not demonstrate transferable systemic delivery of arbitrary folded proteins. Local gastrointestinal medicines and swallowed tissue-injection devices likewise should not be counted as demonstrations of the absorption-based capability defined here.

The available account establishes a March 2026 evidence horizon. The supplied record contains no search evidence establishing developments between that review and November 1, 2026, so it cannot determine whether subsequent advances changed the field. The retained FDA extract ends during page 55 and is partial; it supports the specific pharmacokinetic passages described above but is not an approval letter or a complete regulatory record. Its internal Rybelsus and NDA 213051 identification supports attributing those passages despite an inconsistent cover application number.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed milestone: demonstrate in humans that a common molecular or formulation approach, without device-mediated tissue injection, produces systemic exposure to intact, functional drug matching the clinically relevant exposure profile of an approved injected regimen for at least three structurally unrelated systemically acting proteins, including one monoclonal antibody or cytokine. The studies should distinguish delivery of active protein from detection of fragments or inactive material. Three successes would demonstrate substantial transferability, not applicability to arbitrary proteins.
completion_criteria.label: Common oral approach matches injected exposure across three unrelated proteins

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and usability requirements: repeated-dose studies should characterize variability within and between patients, relevant peaks and troughs, food and water effects, and consistency across manufactured batches. Results should be independently reproduced. Exposure and variability acceptance limits should be specified for each drug according to its therapeutic requirements. Dosing conditions should permit ordinary outpatient use without fasting requirements that critically determine whether an effective dose is absorbed.
completion_criteria.label: Independently reproduce repeated-dose exposure and variability under practical outpatient conditions

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: the absorbed drug should retain biological activity, repeated administration should have acceptable safety, and the required oral dose and formulation should be practical to manufacture and use. Equivalent exposure should not automatically be treated as equivalent efficacy where clinical confirmation is needed. A single modified peptide requiring a large dose to compensate for approximately 1 percent absorption would not meet this breadth criterion, although it could remain a valuable product. Neither the three-protein benchmark nor any particular bioavailability percentage is an established consensus standard.
completion_criteria.label: Oral proteins retain activity with acceptable repeated-dose safety and practicality

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: PHA-05, systemic pharmacological access to brain parenchyma for arbitrary drug classes, shares the challenge of transporting drugs across a biological barrier. PHA-11 concerns entry from the gastrointestinal tract into systemic circulation; PHA-05 concerns subsequent access from circulation to brain tissue. Success at one barrier would not establish success at the other.

Roster-based synthesis: PHA-02, prospective prediction of human efficacy, dose and major toxicity, could help select oral candidates and estimate clinically useful exposure. PHA-11 supplies a delivery capability; PHA-02 supplies predictive capability. Predicting absorption or dose would not itself make a protein orally absorbable, and successful absorption would not establish prospective prediction of human outcomes.

Roster-based synthesis: PHA-13, a medicine that holds its own therapeutic window without an external controller, overlaps with the need for dependable exposure. PHA-11 seeks sufficiently predictable input through oral absorption. PHA-13 seeks intrinsic control of therapeutic action or exposure as conditions change; achieving reliable oral dosing would not by itself provide that control.

Roster-based synthesis: PHA-01, pharmacological control of proteins lacking a usable binding pocket, and PHA-07, dismantling pathogenic protein conformations while restoring function, concern what a medicine can do to its targets. PHA-11 concerns how a peptide or protein medicine reaches systemic circulation. A therapeutic developed under either target-focused concept might benefit from oral delivery, but the delivery breakthrough would not solve target recognition, conformational repair or disease efficacy.

Roster-based synthesis: PHA-03, prevention of idiosyncratic immune-mediated drug injury, remains a distinct safety capability. Preserving protein function and achieving consistent oral exposure would not demonstrate prevention of immune-mediated injury. Immune safety would still require appropriate evaluation for each drug and delivery approach.

change_log.reason: Preserves the useful mechanistic detail while distinguishing successful absorption from reliable therapeutic delivery.

change_log.reason: Semaglutide's exceptional properties do not establish universal exclusion; lack of accumulation alone does not preclude therapeutic exposure.

change_log.change: Separated reduced injection burden from conditional improvements in adherence, access, efficacy and safety.
change_log.reason: Changing administration route does not guarantee clinical superiority or practical benefit.

change_log.change: Retained the approximately 0.4–1 percent semaglutide bioavailability range and one-week half-life while identifying the range as a population-pharmacokinetic estimate.
change_log.reason: Preserves supported quantitative detail and the FDA discussion's limitations on early direct measurements.

change_log.change: Attributed clinical-program histories to the March 2026 review and identified weaknesses in the parathyroid-hormone and growth-hormone references.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence supports a qualified secondary account, without resolving those specific program histories.

change_log.change: Bound the current-state account to the supplied March 2026 evidence and retained the FDA extract's partial-access and document-identification limitations.
change_log.reason: The record does not establish subsequent developments or provide a complete regulatory assessment.

change_log.reason: These requirements address generality and usability while making clear that finite demonstrations establish breadth rather than universality.

unresolved_issues: Developments after March 20, 2026, through November 1, 2026, are not established by the supplied record.
The detailed oral parathyroid-hormone and growth-hormone program histories require better primary-source support; the citation weaknesses do not resolve whether the reported histories are accurate.

The FDA extract is truncated, has an inconsistent cover application number and does not include an approval letter. Its internal identifiers support the specific Rybelsus pharmacokinetic passages, but the complete regulatory record remains unavailable here.
Drug-specific exposure, variability, safety, food-effect and manufacturing acceptance limits remain to be defined for the proposed demonstrations.
The extent to which a shared approach could transfer across structurally diverse proteins remains unknown; three successful demonstrations would not resolve applicability to arbitrary proteins.

brief.title: Protein medicines that work when swallowed
possible: People who depend on injected protein medicines could take more of them by mouth. A shared delivery approach would protect differently shaped medicines through digestion and help them cross the gut lining into the bloodstream, intact and active, at predictable levels.
why: For patients whose treatments could be converted, this would reduce the burden of injections. It could change how many existing medicines are taken, without requiring researchers to find a new treatment target for each disease.

sources.showed: This review describes why swallowed protein medicines often fail and why oral semaglutide succeeds. It attributes that success to the drug’s particular properties, including its long persistence in the body.
sources.cited_for: Oral semaglutide demonstrates useful oral treatment with a peptide, a short protein-like molecule.
sources.not_established: Success with a specially suited drug does not establish a shared delivery approach for differently shaped proteins.

sources.who: Nicholas G. Lamson and colleagues at Carnegie Mellon University
sources.showed: In mice, tiny negatively charged silica particles temporarily loosened barriers between gut-lining cells. Insulin and exenatide given by mouth then lowered blood sugar.
sources.quote: Here, we show that anionic nanoparticles induce tight junction relaxation, increasing intestinal permeability and enabling the oral delivery of proteins.
sources.cited_for: Temporarily loosening the gut barrier enabled swallowed medicines to retain biological activity in mice.
sources.not_established: The mouse results do not establish predictable delivery across diverse proteins or acceptable repeated-dose safety in humans.

sources.who: Inge B. Halberg and colleagues at Novo Nordisk and Profil
sources.showed: A trial in healthy men found that eating immediately after an oral insulin dose substantially reduced absorption. The single-dose treatment was well tolerated.
sources.quote: Oral insulin 338 was well-tolerated with no safety issues identified during the trial.
sources.cited_for: Food timing can strongly affect how much swallowed insulin reaches the bloodstream.
sources.not_established: A single-dose study in healthy men does not establish reliable repeated dosing during ordinary outpatient use.

shown: Oral semaglutide is an approved medicine. As Niazi’s review explains, its potency and long persistence in the body allow it to work despite low and variable absorption.

Carnegie Mellon researchers delivered active insulin and exenatide by mouth in mice using silica particles. Novo Nordisk and Profil tested oral insulin absorption in healthy men, finding that food timing strongly affected it.
missing: A shared approach has yet to deliver diverse intact, active proteins in humans at clinically useful, predictable blood levels.
Independent studies have yet to reproduce reliable repeated dosing under practical eating and drinking conditions.
Broad delivery has yet to combine retained drug activity, acceptable repeated-dose safety and practical manufacturing.

milestones.label: A shared approach matches injections across three unrelated proteins
milestones.explanation: Human studies would have to match injected blood levels over time for three unrelated, intact, active proteins, including an antibody (an immune defence protein) or cytokine (an immune signal). This would test transferability.

milestones.label: Independent studies reproduce reliable dosing in everyday conditions
milestones.explanation: Independent repeated-dose studies would have to reproduce suitable blood levels across patients, batches and practical eating and drinking conditions, without critical fasting requirements. This would establish everyday reliability.

milestones.label: Repeated oral dosing preserves activity, safety and practicality
milestones.explanation: Repeated dosing would have to preserve drug activity, have acceptable safety and use amounts practical to manufacture and take, with clinical benefit confirmed where needed. This would establish usable treatment.

uncertain: How widely could a shared approach transfer across differently shaped proteins, beyond the proposed demonstrations?
Acceptable variation in blood levels, food effects, safety and manufacturing requirements still need drug-specific limits.
The proposed protein benchmark is not a consensus standard, and no single absorption percentage defines success.

page.title: Oral systemic delivery of peptides and folded proteins
page.definition: A shared molecular or formulation approach delivers swallowed peptides and folded proteins across the gut lining into the blood at levels sufficient for treatment. Both must arrive intact and active. For a folded protein, activity depends on its three-dimensional structure. Oral semaglutide illustrates delivery of one peptide: salcaprozate sodium helps it enter the circulation mainly through the stomach lining. Gut-local medicines and swallowed tissue-injection devices are excluded.

goal.need: In a US survey of 2,000 adults prescribed insulin, liraglutide or exenatide for type 2 diabetes, 42% of those still using their injectable medicine cited injection concerns as a barrier to continuing it. An effective oral dose would let patients take that medicine without an injection. A method that works across drugs could extend that choice to people who need other injected medicines. Dosing can still constrain daily life: oral semaglutide requires an empty stomach and a wait of at least 30 minutes before food, drinks or other oral medicines.

figures.caption: Estimated absolute bioavailability of oral semaglutide in the 2025 FDA label.
figures.note: Absolute bioavailability is the fraction of an administered dose reaching systemic circulation. These formulations are not interchangeable milligram for milligram.

completion.title: One delivery approach supports FDA-approved oral treatment with a peptide and a folded protein.
completion.criterion: The same molecular or formulation delivery mechanism is used in a peptide medicine and a structurally distinct folded-protein medicine, and both receive FDA marketing approval for swallowed systemic treatment. Each product's evidence establishes intact active drug exposure, therapeutic efficacy, safety and manufacturing quality under its labelled dosing conditions. Gut-local products and swallowed tissue-injection devices are excluded. This is a minimum demonstration of transfer between cargo classes.
completion.set_by: Atlas operational criterion combining the developers' cross-drug goals with FDA product-level marketing approval.
completion.basis: Searched for oral-protein roadmaps, government-programme targets, regulatory bioavailability limits and cross-cargo criteria, and examined developer goals, FDA drug-review guidance and section 506K. No external completion test for transferable clinical oral delivery was found. FDA approval supplies a product-level decision; section 506K designation requires preliminary evidence of potential reuse. The peptide-plus-folded-protein conjunction is an Atlas criterion.

milestones.title: A swallowed peptide or protein produces its intended systemic effect in a controlled animal study.
milestones.criterion: After oral dosing, the animal shows the intended pharmacological response relative to a negative control under the study's statistical test. For the healthy-mouse insulin experiment in Figure 3 of Lamson et al., the response is a fall in blood glucose and the comparison requires P < 0.05 by a one-tailed t-test. A blood drug concentration alone measures exposure.
milestones.set_by: Controlled animal pharmacology studies of oral insulin and exenatide. Lamson et al. specify the quoted decision rule for their mouse comparison.
milestones.threshold_quote: * p < 0.05 w.r.t. control by one-tailed t-test.

milestones.title: A regulator permits human dosing of an oral peptide or protein after reviewing its supporting evidence.
milestones.criterion: The competent regulator permits a human study of the specific oral product to begin. For a US study under an investigational new drug application, the application takes effect 30 days after FDA receipt unless FDA imposes a clinical hold, or earlier if FDA notifies the sponsor that the study may begin. An ethics committee's decision alone does not establish regulatory permission.
milestones.set_by: US FDA, 21 CFR 312.40(b), for studies under a US investigational new drug application. Other jurisdictions apply their own authorisation rules.
milestones.threshold_quote: Thirty days after FDA receives the IND, unless FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigations described in the IND are subject to a clinical hold

milestones.title: A swallowed peptide or protein reaches a quantifiable concentration in human blood.
milestones.criterion: After oral dosing, a drug-specific assay gives a concentration attributable to the administered drug within its validated quantitative range in human blood, plasma or serum. Apply any stricter rule specified for the study endpoint. In NCT02304627, first appearance of insulin 338 requires a serum concentration above 200 pmol/L. The concentration establishes exposure.
milestones.set_by: International Council for Harmonisation, ICH M10, for the validated assay range. NCT02304627 defines the insulin 338 onset endpoint.
milestones.threshold_quote: The calibration range is defined by the LLOQ, which is the lowest calibration standard, and the ULOQ, which is the highest calibration standard.

milestones.title: A controlled phase 2 study confirms an oral peptide or protein's prespecified efficacy hypothesis.
milestones.criterion: A controlled phase 2 trial meets its prespecified efficacy test for the oral medicine. In NCT01923181, compare the pooled 40 mg standard- and fast-escalation oral semaglutide groups with placebo on change in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) from baseline to week 26. The upper bound of the two-sided 95% confidence interval for the oral-minus-placebo difference must be below zero.
milestones.set_by: Novo Nordisk, NCT01923181 confirmatory analysis. Its numerical efficacy criterion was written for semaglutide; insulin 338 had a separate fasting-glucose endpoint.
milestones.threshold_quote: Efficacy of oral semaglutide was considered confirmed if the upper limit of the 95% CI for the ETD was less than 0

milestones.title: An oral peptide or protein meets its pivotal trial's prespecified efficacy threshold.
milestones.criterion: The oral medicine meets its pivotal trial's prespecified efficacy test. For the PIONEER 4 noninferiority comparison, the upper 95% confidence bound for oral semaglutide minus injected liraglutide on change in HbA1c at week 26 must be below 0.4 percentage points. The primary analysis includes participants regardless of treatment discontinuation or rescue medication. The Chinese ORMD-0801 trial CTR20201644 instead specifies change from baseline in HbA1c at week 24 versus placebo.
milestones.set_by: PIONEER 4 protocol for the semaglutide noninferiority margin. CTR20201644 defines the Chinese oral insulin comparison.

milestones.title: An oral carrier protects its peptide or protein against digestive enzymes in vitro.
milestones.criterion: For a formulation designed to protect a drug from digestion, compare the amount of undegraded drug recovered with and without the carrier under the same enzyme exposure. More intact drug must remain with the carrier. TRANS-INT specified pancreatin for intestinal carriers. A gastric protection assay can use pepsin at acidic pH.
milestones.set_by: TRANS-INT target product profile for intestinal nanocarriers. The pancreatin condition applies to that programme's intestinal assay.
milestones.threshold_quote: The nanocarriers should protect the associated peptide from degradation in the presence of pancreatin.

milestones.title: FDA authorises marketing of one swallowed peptide or folded protein for systemic treatment.
milestones.criterion: FDA approves a drug application or licenses a biological product for a swallowed dosage form with a systemic therapeutic indication. The approval and prescribing information must cover the oral product itself. The route must deliver the drug by absorption across the gut lining.
milestones.set_by: US FDA product approval or biologics licensure, the product-level decisions identified in 21 USC 356k(b)(1).
milestones.threshold_quote: a drug approved under section 355 of this title or a biological product licensed under section 351 of the Public Health Service Act

not_found: No external cross-cargo completion criterion or universal minimum oral bioavailability was located in regulatory, roadmap, government-programme and developer searches.
Complete public nonclinical safety packages and regulator authorisation letters for the cited human studies were not located.
FDA approvals spanning a peptide and a structurally distinct folded protein using the same oral delivery mechanism were not located.
No numerical week-24 primary endpoint result or peer-reviewed efficacy report was located for the 522-participant Chinese ORMD-0801 trial CTR20201644.

results.finding: Oral semaglutide, 632 randomized: week-26 HbA1c difference versus placebo was −1.5 percentage points (95% CI −1.7 to −1.2).
results.detail: The confirmatory comparison pooled the 40-mg standard- and fast-escalation groups; the upper confidence bound was below zero.
results.quote:
At week 26, pooled 40-mg oral semaglutide standard and fast
escalation groups reduced mean HbA 1c level by 1.8% com-
pared with 0.3% with placebo (ETD, –1.5% [95% CI, –1.7% to
–1.2%];P < .001; confirmatory statistical analysis) thus achiev-
ing the primary end point.

results.finding: Enteric-coated insulin capsules released labelled cargo within 15 minutes at intestinal pH (n unreported).
results.detail: The dissolution result characterizes pH-triggered release. How much insulin remained undegraded is unreported.
results.quote: dissolves to provide a burst release of drug within 15 minutes in the pH 5 to 5.5 conditions of mouse small intestine

results.finding: Swallowed insulin with silica lowered blood glucose versus control in healthy mice (n = 5 per group, one-tailed P < 0.05).
results.detail: The qualifying result comes from the oral capsule groups in Figure 3i–j. The paper also reports glucose lowering after oral insulin in diabetic and hyperglycaemic mice.

results.finding: Swallowed exenatide with silica reached 10% relative bioavailability in healthy mice (n = 5 per group).
results.quote: the silica-assisted, orally delivered peptide achieved 10% bioavailability

results.finding: In vitro, the insulin nanocarrier released 50% of its insulin after cellulase or β-glucosidase exposure (n = 3 experiments per group).
results.detail: The release assay quantified radiolabel. The separate mass spectrometry assay characterized the released insulin after hydrolysis without measuring protection against pancreatin or pepsin.

results.finding: Oral nanocarrier insulin lowered blood glucose by up to 13% in fasted, non-diabetic baboons (n = 20).
results.detail: The baboons received the formulation in sugar-free chocolate during insulin tolerance tests that included a zero-dose session. The paper reports a time course and a significance threshold, with no exact P value in the supplied text.
results.quote:
The maximum percentage reduction in blood sugar was observed to be 0%, 5%, 10% and 13% for 1, 2, 5 and 10 IU kg
–1
, respectively.

to the partial clinical hold letter which included the histopathology

results.finding: In CH-ACM-01, oral Mycapssa produced a steady-state octreotide peak concentration of 5.30 ng/mL at the highest daily dose. Sample size unreported.
FDA’s nonclinical reviewers recommended approval of oral Mycapssa for acromegaly under NDA 208232.
results.detail: The review records a recommendation at the nonclinical review stage.
results.quote: Nonclinical Recommendation for Approval.

results.finding: Oral semaglutide was quantifiable in plasma in 100% of the fasting arm (n = 26).
results.detail: The fasting arm took the tablets with 240 mL water after an overnight fast and fasted for 4 hours after dosing.
results.quote: In the fasting group, all subjects had measurable semaglutide exposure.

results.finding: After bedtime ORMD-0801 dosing (n=112), mean morning fasting serum insulin was 114.7 pmol/L.
results.detail: Table 3 gives the numerical serum insulin concentrations. The glucose response is a pharmacodynamic endpoint and does not establish a drug-specific blood concentration.

results.finding: Bedtime ORMD-0801 (n=137 analyzed) reduced the week-4 rise in nighttime glucose versus placebo (P=0.0120).
results.detail: The prespecified analysis excluded the highest and lowest 10% of values by treatment group. Table 2 gives P=0.0117 for the absolute change comparison. Both reported P values meet the prespecified threshold.
results.quote:
mean absolute changes 1.7± 23.5 mg/dL 
and 13.7± 26.1 mg/dL, respectively; p=0.0120

results.finding: Oral semaglutide versus injected liraglutide in PIONEER 4 (711 randomised): upper 95% confidence bound for the HbA1c difference was 0.0 percentage points.
results.quote:
Oral semaglutide was non-inferior to subcutaneous liraglutide in decreasing HbA 1c (estimated treatment 
difference [ETD] −0·1%, 95% CI −0·3 to 0·0; p<0·0001)

results.finding: In SOUL (n = 9,650), oral semaglutide reduced major adverse cardiovascular events versus placebo (hazard ratio 0.86).
results.detail: The intention-to-treat analysis included all randomized participants regardless of adherence or changes to background medications.
results.quote:
placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.86; 95% confidence interval, 0.77 to 0.96; 
P = 0.006).

results.finding: BfArM approved the oral insulin 338 trial protocol. The trial dosed 44 healthy men.
results.quote: The trial protocol was reviewed and approved by the local health authorities (Bundesinstitut für Arzneimittel und Medizinprodukte, Bonn, Germany) and an independent ethics committee (Ethik-Kommission der Ärztekammer Nordrhein, Düsseldorf, Germany).

results.finding: In 44 healthy men dosed with oral insulin 338, the median time to quantifiable serum appearance was 10 minutes.
results.detail: Meals were given immediately or 30, 60 or 360 minutes after dosing. The median time to first quantifiable appearance was the same across conditions.
results.quote:
The median onset of appearance
Ins338
was 10 min independent of post-dose fasting period

results.finding: Exenatide digestion assay (n = 3): 36% remained undegraded with COM nanoparticles after acidic pepsin exposure.
results.detail: Figure 1's caption identifies free exenatide as a comparator, but the supplied text does not identify a matched-time recovery result showing greater recovery with the carrier.
results.quote: For DIS NPs and COM NPs samples, 22% and 36% of the EXE remained undegraded, respectively, even after 4 h of the incubation, indicating that DIS NPs and COM NPs can effectively protect the loaded EXE from digestion in stomach.

results.finding: Oral COM exenatide lowered HbA1c versus saline in db/db mice (n = 6 per group, P < 0.05).
results.quote:
Compared with the 7.95 ± 0.68% of the HbA
1c
concentration of the saline group, the injection, COM NPs and DIS NPs groups decreased their HbA
1c
concentrations to 6.74 ± 0.66% (P < 0.05), 6.79 ± 0.77% (P < 0.05), and 7.08 ± 1.29%, respectively (Fig.
6
b).

results.finding: FDA approved the oral ORMD-0801 study protocol (353 randomized).
results.detail: The sample size follows the Results section, which lists the 20 nonrandomized excipient-only participants separately.
results.quote: The trial protocol was approved by FDA as well as local IRBs of the participating sites

results.finding: Oral ORMD-0801 (353 randomized) yielded no reported drug-specific quantifiable blood concentration at week 12.
results.detail: The paper gives no assay range or method for distinguishing administered insulin from endogenous insulin.
results.quote:
little or no peripheral insulin exposure was detected with ORMD-
0801.

results.finding: Oral ORMD-0801 phase 2 (353 randomized) reported P = 0.021 for the alternative pooled HbA1c comparison.
results.detail: The significant pooled comparison used once- and twice-daily dosing after excluding two sites. The prespecified comparison pooled twice- and three-times-daily dosing.
results.quote:
When analyzing Cohort  A alone the effect of 
the combined 32 mg QD and 32 mg BID vs. combined placebo was significant (p=0.021) .

results.finding: Oral enlicitide (n=2,904) reduced LDL cholesterol by an adjusted 55.8 percentage points more than placebo at week 24.
results.detail: Participants took the sodium caprate formulation fasting and waited 30 minutes before consuming anything other than water. The prespecified analysis used washout imputation for missing data.
results.quote:
representing an adjusted between-group difference of −55.8 percentage points 
(95% CI, −60.9 to −50.7; P<0.001).

results.finding: Oral milk vesicle capsules carrying semaglutide or tirzepatide lowered blood glucose versus control in db/db mice (n = 4–8, P < 0.05).
results.detail: The negative control was semaglutide without SNAC. In a separate experiment, liquid oral semaglutide with or without milk vesicles produced no significant glucose reduction.
results.quote: Both sEV‐semaglutide and sEV‐tirzepatide significantly reduced blood glucose levels compared to the control group

results.finding: Pooled 40-mg oral semaglutide vs placebo (141 vs 71 randomized) met the week-26 HbA1c test with an upper 95% confidence bound of −1.2 percentage points.
results.quote:
At week 26, pooled 40-mg oral semaglutide standard and fast
escalation groups reduced mean HbA 1c level by 1.8% com-
pared with 0.3% with placebo (ETD, –1.5% [95% CI, –1.7% to
–1.2%];P < .001; confirmatory statistical analysis) thus achiev-
ing the primary end point.

results.finding: PLGA-encapsulated liraglutide (n = 3 per condition) had 87.6% recovery after pancreatin exposure, with complete degradation in the free-drug control.
results.detail: The gastric free-drug endpoint is internally inconsistent. The Results report measurable recovery, while the Discussion says none was detected. The intestinal comparison independently meets the criterion.
results.quote: On the other hand, the encapsulation of Lira into PLGA NPs was able to successfully protect 71.2 ± 1.49% and 87.6 ± 1.3% of Lira from degradation in the SGF and SIF at the end of the 2-h incubation, respectively ( Figure 2 ).

results.finding: Human insulin in enteric-coated nanocomplexes (n = 3–4) showed 55% intact insulin remaining after 1 hour of pancreatin exposure, more than free insulin.
results.detail: The intact fractions are calculated from the reported degradation percentages.
results.quote: However, coated PECs conferred some protection: by comparison with the profiles of free insulin and insulin-associated with uncoated PECs, 45% of insulin in coated PECs was degraded at 60 min, with 68% at 120 min.

results.finding: Oral MEDI7219 reduced glucose excursions in insulin-resistant beagles versus placebo (n = 12 treated, 6 placebo, P < 0.01).
results.detail: In Figure 5e, fasted dogs received the oral glucose challenge 90 minutes after their final tablet.
results.quote:
An oral glucose tolerance test performed in fasted dogs postdose on day 14 also revealed significant improvements in glucose excursions in MEDI7219-treated dogs compared with placebo control (
P
< 0.01; Fig.
5
e).

results.finding: Diabetic rats (n = 6 per group) given oral insulin-loaded nanovesicles returned to baseline glucose at 129.3 mg/dl and had significantly better glucose AUC than oral free insulin controls.
results.detail: The rats received an oral glucose challenge 15 minutes after insulin dosing. The supplied text reports significance for the AUC comparison and places the corresponding P values in the figure.
results.quote:
The 
AUC analysis showed that the oral treatment with insulin- loaded 
MiNVs provided a superior blood glucose control, similar to the 
healthy rat, significantly outperforming the other treatment groups 
during the OGTT (Fig. 5H and fig. S28G).

results.finding: FDA authorized one swallowed peptide product, Rybelsus (semaglutide), for systemic glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes.
results.detail: The unit counted is the authorized oral product. September 2019 is the issue date of this Rybelsus label. The heading separately lists 2017 as the initial U.S. approval year for semaglutide.
results.quote:
RYBELSUS is indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 
diabetes mellitus [see Clinical Studies (14.1)].

results.finding: Lipfendra (enlicitide), one swallowed peptide product, received initial U.S. approval in 2026 for systemic LDL cholesterol lowering.
results.quote:
LIPFENDRA® (enlicitide) tablets, for oral use 
Initial U.S. Approval: 2026

definition = "A shared molecular or formulation approach delivers swallowed peptides and folded proteins across the gut lining into the blood at levels sufficient for treatment. Both must arrive intact and active. For a folded protein, activity depends on its three-dimensional structure. Oral semaglutide illustrates delivery of one peptide: salcaprozate sodium helps it enter the circulation mainly through the stomach lining. Gut-local medicines and swallowed tissue-injection devices are excluded.". Reason: The approved semaglutide example identifies the stomach as an absorption site and makes the additional requirement for transfer to a folded protein concrete.

goal.need = "In a US survey of 2,000 adults prescribed insulin, liraglutide or exenatide for type 2 diabetes, 42% of those still using their injectable medicine cited injection concerns as a barrier to continuing it. An effective oral dose would let patients take that medicine without an injection. A method that works across drugs could extend that choice to people who need other injected medicines. Dosing can still constrain daily life: oral semaglutide requires an empty stomach and a wait of at least 30 minutes before food, drinks or other oral medicines.". Reason: The survey quantifies the burden for patients and the dosing instructions show a practical limit on the benefit of switching to tablets.

add statement by TRANS-INT consortium, EU Seventh Framework Programme, 2012: "which could be applied for the delivery of a high number of peptide molecules". Reason: TRANS-INT supplies a public programme objective for reuse across drugs alongside the two company statements.

add milestone after None: "An oral carrier protects its peptide or protein against digestive enzymes in vitro.". Reason: The TRANS-INT target product profile supplies a laboratory test of protection from digestion before systemic activity is tested in animals.

edit m1: title = "A swallowed peptide or protein produces its intended systemic effect in a controlled animal study."; criterion = "After oral dosing, the animal shows the intended pharmacological response relative to a negative control under the study's statistical test. For the healthy-mouse insulin experiment in Figure 3 of Lamson et al., the response is a fall in blood glucose and the comparison requires P < 0.05 by a one-tailed t-test. A blood drug concentration alone measures exposure."; set_by = "Controlled animal pharmacology studies of oral insulin and exenatide. Lamson et al. specify the quoted decision rule for their mouse comparison."; set_by_kind = "community_convention"; threshold_quote = "* p < 0.05 w.r.t. control by one-tailed t-test."; threshold_ref = 6; refs = [6, 20, 28]. Reason: The one-tailed cutoff belongs to a particular mouse experiment, and its exenatide exposure measurement answers a different question from systemic pharmacological activity.

edit m2: criterion = "The competent regulator permits a human study of the specific oral product to begin. For a US study under an investigational new drug application, the application takes effect 30 days after FDA receipt unless FDA imposes a clinical hold, or earlier if FDA notifies the sponsor that the study may begin. An ethics committee's decision alone does not establish regulatory permission."; set_by = "US FDA, 21 CFR 312.40(b), for studies under a US investigational new drug application. Other jurisdictions apply their own authorisation rules."; set_by_kind = "regulator"; threshold_quote = "Thirty days after FDA receives the IND, unless FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigations described in the IND are subject to a clinical hold"; threshold_ref = 30; refs = [30, 7, 8]. Reason: The legal rule identifies when a US investigational new drug application takes effect and distinguishes regulatory permission from ethics-committee approval.

edit m3: title = "A swallowed peptide or protein reaches a quantifiable concentration in human blood."; criterion = "After oral dosing, a drug-specific assay gives a concentration attributable to the administered drug within its validated quantitative range in human blood, plasma or serum. Apply any stricter rule specified for the study endpoint. In NCT02304627, first appearance of insulin 338 requires a serum concentration above 200 pmol/L. The concentration establishes exposure."; set_by = "International Council for Harmonisation, ICH M10, for the validated assay range. NCT02304627 defines the insulin 338 onset endpoint."; set_by_kind = "standards_body"; threshold_quote = "The calibration range is defined by the LLOQ, which is the lowest calibration standard, and the ULOQ, which is the highest calibration standard."; threshold_ref = 31; refs = [31, 8]. Reason: The validated quantitative range includes its lower endpoint, while the insulin 338 protocol used a stricter above-limit rule for time of first appearance.

edit m4: criterion = "A controlled phase 2 trial meets its prespecified efficacy test for the oral medicine. In NCT01923181, compare the pooled 40 mg standard- and fast-escalation oral semaglutide groups with placebo on change in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) from baseline to week 26. The upper bound of the two-sided 95% confidence interval for the oral-minus-placebo difference must be below zero."; threshold_quote = "Efficacy of oral semaglutide was considered confirmed if the upper limit of the 95% CI for the ETD was less than 0"; threshold_ref = 9; refs = [9]. Reason: The efficacy rule needs its prespecified treatment groups and comparator, while the observed effect sizes belong with the results.

edit m5: criterion = "The oral medicine meets its pivotal trial's prespecified efficacy test. For the PIONEER 4 noninferiority comparison, the upper 95% confidence bound for oral semaglutide minus injected liraglutide on change in HbA1c at week 26 must be below 0.4 percentage points. The primary analysis includes participants regardless of treatment discontinuation or rescue medication. The Chinese ORMD-0801 trial CTR20201644 instead specifies change from baseline in HbA1c at week 24 versus placebo."; set_by = "PIONEER 4 protocol for the semaglutide noninferiority margin. CTR20201644 defines the Chinese oral insulin comparison."; set_by_kind = "protocol"; threshold_quote = "non-inferiority [margin: 0\u00b74%]"; threshold_ref = 18; refs = [18, 32]. Reason: The pivotal criterion mixes observed results with its decision rule and omits the different assessment time in the Chinese insulin protocol.

add milestone after m5: "FDA authorises marketing of one swallowed peptide or folded protein for systemic treatment.". Reason: Approval of one oral product is a distinct step between pivotal efficacy and demonstration of the same delivery mechanism in two approved cargo classes.
